31 Four diagrams representing the electric field between two oppositely-charged point charges are
shown.
Which diagram correctly shows the electric field lines?
A
B
+
–
+
–
C
D
+
–
+
–

hints: Notice the $+$ charge on the left and the $-$ charge on the right and check which way each arrowhead points at the ends of the lines.
Recall that electric field direction is the direction a positive test charge would move: away from $+$ and towards $-$.
Compare the far-left horizontal line and the far-right horizontal line with the curved lines joining the charges - all arrows must run from $+$ to $-$.
walkthrough: Identify the charges: positive point charge on the left, negative point charge on the right.
State the governing rule: electric field lines start on positive charge and end on negative charge, and never cross.
Check the central straight line: it must point from left to right, from $+$ to $-$.
Check the outer lines on the left: they must point away from the $+$ charge, to the left and outward.
Check the outer lines on the right: they must point towards the $-$ charge, to the left and inward, and the curved lines between the charges must go from $+$ to $-$.
Only the diagram where every arrowhead follows the $+$ to $-$ sense satisfies all these checks. This is option A.

A.explanation: All lines leave the $+$ charge and enter the $-$ charge, including the central line and the curved outer lines. This matches the rule for direction of electric field.

B.explanation: The outer lines on the left of the $+$ charge have arrows pointing into the $+$ charge, which would mean field lines end on positive charge.

C.explanation: The outer lines on the left point into the $+$ charge instead of out of it, so the lines do not all start on positive and end on negative.

D.explanation: The outer lines on the right of the $-$ charge have arrows pointing away from the $-$ charge, which would mean field lines start on negative charge.
